text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- John Koech, who on Friday resigned as minister of state in the office of the president, withdraws his decision citing pressure from his constituents and counsel from the president.
- The government publishes the Constitution of Kenya Review Commission Bill seeking to establish a commission to overhaul the constitution.
- Flights are delayed for up to six hours or diverted from Kenya's main airports by a go-slow by air traffic controllers.
- Air traffic controllers on Monday threaten to ground all airport operations across the country.
- President Daniel arap Moi meets with religious leaders who urge him to hold dialogue with all parties concerned in the constitutional reform process.
- The government assures Kenyans the economic situation in the country is under control despite suspension of aid by the International Monetary Fund.
- Moslem legislators and officials of the national trade union body urge the National Convention Executive Council to call off a national strike on Friday.
- The Minister for Lands & Settlement Noah Katana Ngala says the decision by the IMF to suspend a key aid package was unfortunate.
- The Chairman of Lonrho East Africa Mark Too says the decision by the IMF was a malicious and politically motivated game of double standards aimed at hurting millions of poor Kenyans.
